- When sentiment turns negative in the last 3–5 days, reduce forecasted price momentum; avoid over-optimistic rebounds.
- If recent price history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive downward moves), model should not over-forecast recovery.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model tends to overshoot — cap forecasted peak at 1–2% below prior high.
- If sentiment is consistently bullish (last 5+ days >0.5), model should not over-forecast downward moves — avoid “sell-off” bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent trend persistence.
- When sentiment flips from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model should reduce forecast slope — avoid “sudden reversal” overfitting.
- If model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon (e.g., first 7 days), apply a 1–2% downward bias to first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (e.g., alternating +1/-1), model should smooth forecast curve — avoid “noise amplification” in price swings.
